questions.stem: Which city serves as the official capital of New Zealand, often confused with its largest city?

options.option_text: Auckland, the most populous city and commercial hub of New Zealand
Wellington, the seat of Parliament and government of New Zealand
Christchurch, the largest city on the South Island of New Zealand
Hamilton, a major inland city in the Waikato region of New Zealand

questions.explanation: Wellington is New Zealand's capital and hosts Parliament, the Supreme Court, and all government ministries. Auckland is the most frequent wrong answer because it is the largest and best-known city internationally — but it has never been the capital.

questions.stem: Switzerland is geographically located in the heart of Europe yet does not use the Euro. What is Switzerland's official currency?

options.option_text: Euro — the shared currency adopted by most European Union nations
Swiss Franc (CHF) — Switzerland is not a member of the European Union
Austrian Schilling — the pre-Euro currency that Austria once used
Swedish Krona — the currency retained by non-Eurozone EU member Sweden

questions.explanation: Switzerland uses the Swiss Franc (CHF). Despite being surrounded by EU member states, Switzerland is NOT an EU member and therefore not part of the Eurozone. Euro is the most tempting distractor precisely because of Switzerland's central European location.

questions.stem: The currency 'Forint' is the official currency of which country?

options.option_text: Romania — an EU member state in southeastern Europe since 2007
Hungary — a landlocked Central European nation and EU member state
Bulgaria — located on the Balkan Peninsula in southeastern Europe
Czech Republic — a Central European nation that borders Germany

questions.explanation: The Hungarian Forint (HUF) is the currency of Hungary. All four options are EU members that have not yet adopted the Euro, making this a genuine test of recall. Romania uses the Leu, Bulgaria uses the Lev, and Czech Republic uses the Koruna — all classic exam mix-ups.

questions.stem: Dodoma was officially designated Tanzania's capital in 1996, replacing which city that still remains Tanzania's largest city and economic hub?

options.option_text: Mwanza, located on the southern shore of Lake Victoria in Tanzania
Dar es Salaam, the historic Indian Ocean coastal port city of Tanzania
Arusha, the northern city near Mount Kilimanjaro and the Serengeti
Zanzibar Town, the main city of the semi-autonomous Zanzibar archipelago

questions.explanation: Dar es Salaam was Tanzania's de facto capital before Dodoma was officially designated in 1996 to shift power inland. Dar es Salaam remains the largest city and financial centre. Arusha is a popular distractor as it hosts the East African Community headquarters.

questions.stem: The 'Ngultrum' is the official currency of which South Asian country?

options.option_text: Nepal — the Himalayan nation known for Mount Everest and trekking routes
Bhutan — the Land of the Thunder Dragon in the Eastern Himalayas
Maldives — the low-lying archipelago nation spread across the Indian Ocean
Sri Lanka — the teardrop-shaped island nation situated south of India

questions.explanation: The Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN) is the official currency of Bhutan, pegged 1:1 to the Indian Rupee. Nepal uses the Nepalese Rupee, Maldives uses the Rufiyaa, and Sri Lanka uses the Sri Lankan Rupee — all highly plausible wrong answers in SAARC-currency questions.

questions.stem: Which of the following country–currency pairings is INCORRECTLY matched?

options.option_text: Oman — Rial Omani, one of the highest-valued currencies in the world
Kuwait — Dirham, used widely across Gulf Cooperation Council states
Bahrain — Dinar, subdivided into 1,000 fils like several Gulf currencies
Qatar — Riyal, the official currency of this Gulf peninsula nation

questions.explanation: Kuwait uses the Kuwaiti Dinar (KWD), NOT the Dirham. The Dirham is the currency of the UAE (AED) and Morocco (MAD). The pairing 'Kuwait — Dirham' is incorrect. Oman–Rial, Bahrain–Dinar, and Qatar–Riyal are all correctly matched, making B the incorrect pair.

questions.stem: The currency 'Lempira' is named after a 16th-century Lenca indigenous chief who led armed resistance against Spanish colonizers. Which country uses the Lempira as its official currency?

options.option_text: Guatemala — where the Quetzal currency is named after the sacred Mayan bird
Honduras — a Central American nation bordered by Guatemala and Nicaragua
Nicaragua — where the Córdoba replaced older Spanish colonial currency units
El Salvador — which adopted the US Dollar as its sole legal tender in 2001

questions.explanation: Honduras uses the Lempira (HNL), named after the Lenca chief Lempira who resisted Spanish conquest in the 1530s. Guatemala uses the Quetzal, Nicaragua uses the Córdoba, and El Salvador officially dollarised in 2001. The historical eponym angle is a classic PYQ-style hard question.
